page: Amazon Web Services c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7a.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance, placing in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Its cryptographic and vector capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI, which contribute to its strong performance in Passmark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached reads and large-block writes rank in the top 25%, large-block uncached reads and overall Passmark memory scores fall into the average tier.

For specialized workloads, the instance excels in LLM inference prompt processing for small models, reaching top-tier performance. It also delivers strong results in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that require high-frequency dedicated cores and DDR5 memory speeds without the overhead of local storage or GPU accelerators. Appropriate workloads include high-performance web serving, database operations, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
